how_i_measured: Copied app/, docs/, assets/, seed/, tools/, evidence/scenes+coldstart.json to /tmp/lt-code-critic and ran the suite there so nothing in the repository moved: `flutter test --no-pub` from /tmp/lt-code-critic/app. Result: 160 test cases, exit 0, 'All tests passed!' (/tmp/lt-test-final.txt:229). This matters because two tests write into ../evidence/ when the suite runs in place (coldstart_test.dart:27, reliability_test.dart:344).

Re-ran module_costs_test's scan myself in Python over lib/**.dart + web/**{js,json,html} for every module id, event type and renderer id: zero offenders in scope. Extended it to android/**.kt|xml, tools/**.py and seed/**.py, which the test does not scan: the only hits are seed/tools/validate.py:54-55,200-202.
Compared docs/EVENT_TYPES.md's table to kEventTypes by regex, element by element: 18 == 18, identical order, identical ids.

Scanned every blob in git history under 1.5 MB (4,731 of them, via `git cat-file --batch-all-objects`) for tskey-*, TS_AUTHKEY=, BEGIN * PRIVATE KEY, BEGIN CERTIFICATE, AWS_SECRET. Zero matches. Also swept all 623 tracked non-binary files for base64 runs of 60+ chars. Zero. Commit history was read as file-path lists only (`git log --format=%H --name-only`), never as messages.
Walked assets/ on disk (745 files) against assets/MANIFEST.json (749 entries), applying tools/check/manifest.py's own exemption list.
Probed the persistence_boundary_test regex against nine import forms in Python to find what it catches and what it does not.

rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store: any file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build
rules.evidence: The boundary itself is real and correctly drawn. sqlite3 is imported in exactly one file (app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10), idb_shim in exactly one (app/lib/spine/store/store_web.dart:4); everything above them sees only the abstract SpineStore (app/lib/spine/store/store.dart:17-40), and app/lib/spine/store/open_store.dart:8-10 is the single place that names a platform. My own grep for sqflite|sqlite|hive|shared_preferences|idb_shim|indexed_db|localStorage|isar|objectbox|drift across app/lib found no driver import outside lib/spine/store/; path_provider appears in app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:5 and read_bytes_io.dart:5 but that is a directory lookup, not a store. app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:16-30 enforces it, and enforces it twice (a second test at :32-42 keeps drivers under store/ even inside spine/). Two gaps. (a) The regex at persistence_boundary_test.dart:7-10 requires the package URI to follow `import`/`export` immediately: I fed it nine forms and it catches plain single- and double-quoted imports, exports, `deferred as`, a line-broken import and `dart:html`, but MISSES `import 'stub.dart' if (dart.library.io) 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';`. That is not a hypothetical shape — it is the idiom this codebase uses in ten places (app/lib/media/read_bytes.dart:4, media/local_uri.dart:4, ready.dart:2, capture/hooks.dart:24, transport/tailscale/proxy_client.dart:9, transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:12, setup/platform.dart:6, ambient/ambient.dart:23, spine/store/open_store.dart:9-10), so it is the first thing anyone adding a platform-specific driver would reach for, and it would pass. (b) Nothing in the repository runs the suite: there is no .github/ or other CI directory, and `flutter test` appears in none of run.sh, capture.sh, bootstrap.sh or tools/critics.sh. 'Fails the build' is true only if a person types it.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, docs and code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list
rules.evidence: Eighteen types, comfortably over the floor: app/lib/spine/types.dart:127-331 (ids at lines 127,139,153,166,179,193,205,217,228,240,251,262,274,285,297,308,320,331). I extracted every EventTypeSpec and confirmed all eighteen carry a non-null renderer, notify, search, noun and announced — none missing. Doc and code agree on the list: docs/EVENT_TYPES.md rows 1-18 parsed by the same regex the test uses give exactly the registry's ids in exactly the registry's order. app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 asserts equality of the two lists plus >= 14 plus uniqueness; app/test/thread_types_test.dart:17-24 and :26-32 close the renderer loop in both directions against kThreadRenderers (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:165-180); :50-68 asserts every type reads as a sentence rather than a registry id; :90-108 derives 'is this a margin line' from the registry rather than from a fourth list. Search is registry-driven for real: app/lib/spine/search.dart:31,51,58,69,76 index off spec.search.textFields / .facets / .excluded, and the search page's 'found as' line reads spec.noun (app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:425). The service worker keeps no per-type table of its own — app/web/push/sw.js:144-153 reads only `kind` and `from` off the push and looks the words up in a table the app writes into the store (sw.js:130-138). The failure: two rows of the doc's notification column describe behaviour the code does not have. docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:44 says date_event is 'per action; quiet for planned, interruptive for scheduled' and :45 says todo_event is 'quiet; interruptive when assigned to you'. The registry says Notify.quiet flat for both (app/lib/spine/types.dart:265, :277), and the only consumer, NotificationPrefs.forType (app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:78-82), keys on the type id alone — there is no branch anywhere on action or on assignee (`assignee` appears in app/lib only in the todos module's own rendering and payload, never in a notification path). spine_schema_test compares the id lists and nothing else, so the drift in the treatment column is unheld. Smaller: app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:526-531 still keeps a hand-written set of seven renderer ids to decide what is paper — the polarity is right (new types default to paper, so a module costs nothing) but it is a fourth place a new mark-shaped messenger type must be added, and docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:55-70 says three steps and 'Nothing else changes'.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line; the commit that added the fourth touched nothing under the first three
rules.evidence: The registry is one const list of five (app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16). Every consumer iterates it generically and none names a module: thread bodies are spread from kModules (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:179), the sentence table asks the modules last (:223), paper stock comes from the module (app/lib/material/assignment.dart:35), the Us desk budget is built from m.rowHeight and m.share (app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:42-45,85-93), search facets from m.label/m.eventTypes (app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:61), and the capture hooks from m.eventTypes (app/lib/capture/hooks.dart:534,542). The interface carries everything that used to be a shared table: stocks, bodies, sentence, share, rowHeight (app/lib/modules/module.dart:63-107). app/test/module_costs_test.dart:35-77 forbids every handle a shared file could key off — the module id, its event types, and the renderer the registry names for each — anywhere outside that module's directory, over .dart and over web/*.js|json|html; I re-ran that scan independently and got zero offenders in scope. app/test/module_costs_test.dart:79-99 additionally asserts each module's own body is the one the thread actually uses (identical(), not just non-null), and :101-127 that its sentence is what summaryOf returns. On the historical half: the fourth module has no commit of its own to check — calendar and rituals are both present in the initial commit d2be5a3d. The fifth does: shelf arrived in ffc5821d, whose complete file list is app/lib/modules/shelf/shelf_module.dart (new, +180), app/lib/modules/registry.dart (+2), app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart (+7), app/lib/spine/types.dart (+8), docs/EVENT_TYPES.md, seed/tools/validate.py and eleven seed/year/*.jsonl. Nothing under dates/, todos/, calendar/ or rituals/ — the rule's actual test, and it passes. Of the three shared code files it touched then, one is gone (regions/chat/renderers.dart no longer exists; the table moved to app/lib/thread/renderers.dart and is assembled from kModules), one is registry.dart's one line, and one is the spine registry, which app/lib/modules/module.dart:12-16 argues is a principle rather than a cost and I agree: a module inventing its own schema is what a single spine forbids. The only remaining out-of-repo-code cost I found is seed/tools/validate.py:54-55, which carries a per-type payload table the module_costs scan does not cover — and it is a corpus validator, not shipped code.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events
rules.evidence: They are a different type in a different place. Ephemeral (app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-146) is not an Event and has no path into the spine: the host's handler passes it straight to a callback and returns 204 (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:264-269), the pull response carries it in a field the client drains into a stream (server_io.dart:211-217, http_transport.dart:250-255), and AppScope._onEphemeral (app/lib/scope.dart:153-165) sets a bool with a six-second timer and calls notifyListeners — it never touches spine.append. The one way anything is written is AppScope.emit → Spine.append (scope.dart:170-171), and Spine.append's first act is `specOf(type)` (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:220), which throws ArgumentError for any id not in the registry (app/lib/spine/types.dart:346-350). 'typing' and 'presence' are not in the registry, so they cannot be appended even by mistake. Two tests hold it: app/test/transport_local_test.dart:287-303 sends a typing frame client→host and a presence frame host→client, checks both arrive, then asserts `r.host.length == 0` and `r.client.length == 0` — the strong form; and app/test/reliability_test.dart:119-130 records the same as a capability and reliability_test.dart:352 asserts every capability's ok is true. docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:28-29 names the four ephemeral kinds explicitly.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread
rules.evidence: Three independent things would each have to break. (a) The projection returns before the row is added: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:279-286 handles 'read_marker' by moving _readUpto and returning, and the generic guard `if (!spec.rowInThread) return;` at :286 catches it again from the registry. (b) The registry says so: rowInThread: false at app/lib/spine/types.dart:225 (and for reaction, message_edit, message_delete at :190, :202, :214). (c) The renderer it names is a no-op: 'ink_dries' maps to _neverARow in app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:174. Tests: app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34 asserts rowInThread is false for read_marker and reaction; app/test/thread_types_test.dart:112-120 asserts it again from the registry; app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart:55-59 replays a log containing a read_marker and asserts no thread item has that type while readUpto is populated — which is the behavioural form, not just the flag.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file, history included
rules.evidence: Nothing. I read every blob in the object database under 1.5 MB — 4,731 of them, covering every tracked text file that has ever existed — through grep for `tskey-auth-*`, `tskey-` runs, `TS_AUTHKEY=<value>`, `BEGIN (RSA|EC|ENCRYPTED|OPENSSH)? PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN CERTIFICATE` and AWS_SECRET: zero matches. A separate sweep of all 623 tracked non-binary files for base64-looking runs of 60+ characters returned one hit, a URL comment in app/pubspec.yaml:16. TS_AUTHKEY appears by name only as an environment variable and as a status word: bootstrap.sh:217-221 writes 'present'/'pending' to a file and never the value, tools/tailscale/up.sh:48-60,109 reads it from the environment. The only PEM material on this disk is under toolchain/ (vendored Flutter and pub test fixtures), and /toolchain/ is the first line of .gitignore; `git ls-files toolchain` is empty. The pairing secret is minted at runtime from Random.secure (app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:44-47) and the six words are never stored — only the derived key (wire.dart:75-79); the capture harness writes them to $TMPDIR/lovetap-capture/pair.json (capture.sh:26,177), outside the tree, and no path matching pair.json has ever been committed. The VAPID private key comes from an env var (tools/push/webpush.py:211); evidence/logs/webpush.txt records that a header was formed, not the key. coldstart_test.dart:39-40 says in a comment that the auth key is not in tailscaled's status output and must never be committed, and evidence/coldstart.json carries node public keys only.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key
rules.evidence: The bind is the strongest thing in the transport. app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-32 defines a tailnet address as 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 and nothing else; addressToServeOn (:57-74) checks a declared address rather than trusting it and throws NotOnTheTailnet when there is none — there is no fallback branch, and TailscaleBinding.hostBind (app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:70-77) is the only producer of a HostBind for that transport. The client refuses to talk to a non-tailnet host too (tailscale_transport.dart:82-93). app/test/tailnet_test.dart:12-31 asserts 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.x, 10.x, '::', fe80::, 100.63.255.255 and 100.128.0.0 are all rejected; :33-45 that declaring any of the first four throws; :47-63 that with no tailnet there is a reason and not a fallback. evidence/reliability.json's tailscale block records a real run: host_reachable_at 100.68.254.25, host_reachable_at_is_tailnet true, and the loopback listener explained as the userspace-tailscaled case, which is narrower than the tailnet address rather than wider. Auth: app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:96-102 rejects with 401 and an empty body before dispatching anything, for every /v1 route except the two pairing calls, which cannot be signed by construction; _authenticated (:126-141) checks the device id against the pairing, a five-minute skew, an HMAC-SHA256 over method+path+ts+nonce+sha256(body) compared in constant time (wire.dart:96-107), and a replay-nonce cache (wire.dart:128-145). The push path additionally refuses an event authored as somebody the pairing does not cover (server_io.dart:232-236). app/test/transport_local_test.dart:74-91 asserts an unpaired pull throws, that wrong words are refused, and that right words pair. One note rather than a fault: _serveStatic (server_io.dart:304-328) answers unauthenticated GETs, but only from pwaRoot, and pwaRoot is null in the shipped app (app/lib/main.dart:76-88 never sets it) — only the capture daemon passes one (app/tool/host_daemon.dart:105,109). In the app as built, every non-/v1 request is a 404. Traversal is guarded at server_io.dart:312-317.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font came off the internet
rules.evidence: 745 files under assets/ on disk; 749 entries in assets/MANIFEST.json; every entry has a non-empty generator field (I checked all 749). The only three files with no entry are assets/MANIFEST.json itself, assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json and assets/tears/relief.json, which are the manifest and two generator sidecars and are named in tools/check/manifest.py:24-25's exemption list; that leaves 740 real assets, 740 covered, which is what evidence/logs/manifest.json records ('files': 740, 'without_an_entry': [], 'ok': true) and what I get independently. The generators are ten scripts, all in this repository: blender/{bits/bits.py, folds/fold.py, objects/objects.py, paper/stocks.py, paper/tear_relief.py, shell/desk.py} and tools/{handwriting/build.py, ink_plate.py, sound/synth.py, tears/tear.py}. The three fonts are generated, not downloaded: assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json names tools/handwriting/build.py as generator and its inputs as two hashed JSON files in the repo (tools/handwriting/hands.json, tools/handwriting/skeletons.json), with per-face skeleton and pen parameters rather than a source face. No generator touches the network — my grep for urllib/requests/socket./http.client/wget/curl across tools/ and blender/ returned only the word 'curl' meaning curled paper (blender/paper/tear_relief.py:41,87, blender/folds/fold.py:249, etc.); the single real network user is tools/push/webpush.py, which sends a push and downloads nothing (its self-test posts to https://push.example.net). Two blemishes, neither a rule breach: seven entries name files written to /tmp/tear* scratch directories that are not and never were part of the library (assets/MANIFEST.json, keys beginning '../../../tmp/'), and tools/check/manifest.py:76-96's --fill mode can synthesise an entry for a file by copying its parent directory's entry, so a generator that recorded only the directory gets coverage it did not itself write.

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to
rules.evidence: They pass. I ran them: 160 cases, exit 0, no skips (`skip:` appears nowhere in app/test/), and the suite is substantial — 53 test files, 156 test/testWidgets declarations, 465 expect()/expectLater() calls, and no file with zero assertions (lowest density is nothing_is_drawn_by_the_diagnostic_test.dart at two tests and one shared assertion, and that one is a real check on resolved TextStyle decoration). Several are stronger than their names: nothing_moves_on_the_wall_clock_test.dart:52-72 greps the source for thirteen implicit-animation widgets and for AnimationController in files that have never heard of DrivenClock; module_costs_test.dart reads the source because the claim is about the source; reliability_test.dart:352 asserts every one of nineteen capabilities is ok rather than merely reporting them. Three failures of the second clause. (a) app/test/coldstart_test.dart:68-107 — 'cold start over the tailnet: four events, both directions, both spines agreeing' — returns after writing a 'pending' JSON file, with zero assertions executed, whenever the two tailscaled sockets do not answer. It is green in that state; it was green in my run, where toolchain/ts/ did not exist at all. The reasoning at :75-90 for not overwriting a dated run is sound, but the test should be skipped, not passed. (b) app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart:62-69 — 'every module reads the same log and says something from it' — passes for the shelf module against a fixture log (:96-140) that contains no passed_on event at all; ShelfModule.glance returns the empty-state string 'nothing passed on yet' (app/lib/modules/shelf/shelf_module.dart:53-55), which is non-empty, so the assertion holds while proving nothing about that module. The fixture covers 13 of the 18 types; video, voice_note, passed_on, ping and feeling_authored are absent. (c) docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:98 states that this test 'replays the seeded year and compares every region's view to a golden'. It replays a sixteen-event hand-written log against a second replay of itself; there is no seeded year in it and no golden file anywhere in app/test/. The test's own header is honest about what it does; the document is not. Fourth, smaller: running the suite in place writes ../evidence/coldstart.json (coldstart_test.dart:27,98) and ../evidence/reliability.json (reliability_test.dart:344) — the suite is also an evidence generator, so a test run and a capture are not separable by timestamp.

findings.what: bootstrap_page.dart's two functions — mobileConfig() and bootstrapPage(), 105 lines that build the iPhone's CA profile and the page that hands it over — are called by nothing: grep for 'bootstrap_page', 'bootstrapPage' and 'mobileConfig' across app/lib, app/test and app/tool returns only their own definitions, no route serves /setup/profile.mobileconfig, no SecurityContext is ever constructed so server_io.dart:62 always takes the plain HttpServer.bind branch, and main.dart never passes pwaRoot, so the shipped app 404s every request outside /v1.
findings.why: docs/PHONES.md step 3 tells the reader to open the host's address in Safari to add the web app, and step 4 says 'The host serves over HTTPS with a certificate it made itself' — an install path for the Apple half of the brief that no code in the app performs; the only thing that serves the PWA is python3 -m http.server on the dev machine (run.sh:110-112), so the coherence between what the app is documented to do and what it does is broken at the seam where the second device gets the app.

findings.what: The registry table says date_event announces itself 'per action; quiet for planned, interruptive for scheduled' and todo_event 'quiet; interruptive when assigned to you'; the registry entries are Notify.quiet flat, and NotificationPrefs.forType keys on the type id alone with no branch anywhere on action or assignee.
findings.why: Rule 2 requires the document and the code to agree on each type's notification treatment, and the test that is cited as holding them together (spine_schema_test.dart:8-18) compares only the list of ids, so two cells of that column can drift and have.

findings.what: The driver regex requires the package URI to follow `import`/`export` directly, so it misses `import 'stub.dart' if (dart.library.io) 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';` — I probed it with nine forms and this is the one that gets through — while the codebase reaches every platform-specific implementation with exactly that idiom in ten files.
findings.why: The single-store rule is the one the brief says must fail the build, and the guard has a hole shaped precisely like the way somebody would add a second store.

findings.what: The test named 'cold start over the tailnet: four events, both directions, both spines agreeing' writes a 'pending' file and returns before any expect() runs when the two tailscaled sockets do not answer, and reports as a pass.
findings.why: A green test that asserted nothing is the case rule 9 names; markTestSkipped would say the same thing honestly, and evidence/coldstart.json already carries the dated real run it is protecting.

findings.what: 'every module reads the same log and says something from it' passes for the shelf module on a fixture log containing no passed_on event, because ShelfModule.glance returns 'nothing passed on yet' (shelf_module.dart:55); and the document claims this test 'replays the seeded year and compares every region's view to a golden' when it replays a sixteen-event hand-written log against itself and there is no golden file in the repository.
findings.why: The assertion is weaker than its name for one of five modules, and the document's description is weaker still — a reader checking the projection claim would find a citation that does not do what it says.

findings.where: run.sh, capture.sh, bootstrap.sh, tools/critics.sh; app/test/coldstart_test.dart:27; app/test/reliability_test.dart:344
findings.what: Nothing in the repository runs the test suite — there is no CI directory and `flutter test` appears in none of the four scripts — and when it is run in place two tests write into ../evidence/.
findings.why: Rules 1, 2, 4, 5 and the extensibility guard in module_costs_test all rest on the suite being run, so 'fails the build' is a claim about a human habit rather than about the build; and a suite that writes artifacts makes a test run and a capture indistinguishable in evidence/MANIFEST.json.

findings.where: the seven entries whose keys begin '../../../tmp/tear'
findings.what: Seven manifest entries name files written into /tmp scratch directories during tear smoke tests; they are records of things that were never in assets/, and evidence/logs/manifest.json lists them under entries_without_a_file alongside two false positives (fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json and tears/tears.json, which exist but are exempt, so the stale check reports them as missing).
findings.why: The manifest is the record that nothing in the library arrived from somewhere unaccounted for; entries for files that were never in it make the record say more than it knows, and tools/check/manifest.py:60-71 already has a --fill path that would drop them.

what_is_working: The single spine is real, not asserted. One driver per platform in one directory (store_sqlite.dart:10, store_web.dart:4), one abstract interface above it, one append path that validates every payload against the registry before it writes (spine.dart:220-222) and before it takes one off the wire (server_io.dart:239-242), and a projection layer that spine_replay_golden_test shows is order-independent, prefix-composable, and loses everything an event loses.

The module registry genuinely costs a directory and a line now. I re-ran module_costs_test's source scan myself over lib/ and web/ for every module id, event type and renderer id and got zero offenders; every consumer of kModules iterates it (renderers.dart:179,223, assignment.dart:35, us_region.dart:42-93, search_page.dart:61, hooks.dart:534,542) and the interface carries stocks, bodies, sentence, share and rowHeight so none of those is a shared table any more. The test also checks identity, not just presence — identical(kThreadRenderers[r], m.bodies[r]) — which is the version that cannot be satisfied by declaring a body nothing uses.

Eighteen event types against a floor of fourteen, with the document and the registry byte-identical on ids and order, and three tests holding renderer, sentence and marginality to the registry from three directions so no fourth list can appear.

The tailnet bind is the tightest code in the repository: one predicate for what a tailnet address is, no fallback path to anything else, a declared address checked rather than trusted, the client refusing off-tailnet peers too, and eight named wrong answers asserted in tailnet_test.

The pairing auth is properly built — HKDF-SHA256 from six spoken words, per-request HMAC over method, path, timestamp, nonce and body hash, constant-time compare, a bounded nonce cache against replay, and a 401 with an empty body before any handler is reached.
No secret anywhere, in the tree or in 4,731 history blobs, and the harness keeps the pairing words in a scratch directory outside the repository.
740 assets, 740 entries, ten generators all in this repository, three fonts built from parameters rather than downloaded, and no generator that can reach the network.

160 tests pass, none skipped, and the suite reaches for source-level guards (the wall-clock animation grep, the module-handle scan, the storage-driver scan) rather than only widget assertions — which is the right instinct for rules that are structural.
verdict: The architecture the brief asks for is here and it is measurably here rather than claimed: one event log with one driver per platform behind one interface, eighteen types in a registry the document matches element for element, five shared-life modules that a sixth could join with a directory and a line — I re-ran the test's own source scan and found nothing outside a module's directory naming that module, and the fifth module's actual commit touched nothing under the first four. Typing never reaches the log and two tests say so behaviourally; read markers cannot become rows through any of the three places that would have to fail; the host binds a tailnet address or refuses to start; every /v1 request is signed and replay-protected; there is no secret in the working tree or in any of 4,731 blobs of history; and every one of 740 assets names one of ten in-repo generators, none of which can reach the network. The suite runs green at 160 cases with nothing skipped. What keeps this at the floor rather than above it is a set of seams where the claim is ahead of the code. The largest is that docs/PHONES.md describes the Android phone serving the iPhone its web app over HTTPS with a self-made certificate, and the file that would do half of that — bootstrap_page.dart, 105 lines of CA profile and handover page — is imported by nothing, no SecurityContext is ever constructed, and the shipped app never sets pwaRoot, so it answers 404 to everything outside /v1; the only thing that serves the PWA is a python http.server in run.sh. Around it: two rows of the registry's notification column promise per-action and per-assignee interruption that no code implements, and the test cited as holding document and code together compares only the list of ids; the storage-driver guard misses the conditional-import form this codebase itself uses in ten files; the tailnet cold-start test passes with zero assertions executed when there is no tailnet; the replay test's 'every module says something' passes for the shelf on a log with none of the shelf's events; and nothing in the repository actually runs the suite, so 'fails the build' names a habit rather than a gate. None of that is structural rot — the spine, the registry and the module boundary are the best things in this build and they would survive a sixth module without rework. It is the difference between a system that is coherent and a system whose documents are coherent with it.
